---
title: "validation & leakage prevention"
---

## two meanings of validation

- **data validation:** check whether inputs meet the expected contract
- **model validation:** assess whether a candidate performs well enough for its intended use
- a table can pass every schema check and still contain leaked information

::: {.table-responsive tabindex="0"}

| check | example | response |
|---|---|---|
| schema | required columns and numeric types | stop on incompatible inputs |
| completeness | missing identifiers or excessive missing features | stop or quarantine according to the contract |
| uniqueness | duplicate event keys | investigate; repeated entity ids may be legitimate |
| validity | impossible dates or unexpected categories | reject or quarantine affected records |
| freshness | a daily source has not updated | alert and investigate before using stale inputs |
| distribution | a feature distribution changes | investigate context and impact |

:::

## start with explicit checks

- suppose `df` is a labelled training table with `record_id`, `amount`, and binary `target`
- this toy contract allows missing amounts for later imputation, but rejects invalid observed values and missing labels

```python
from pandas.api.types import is_numeric_dtype

required = {"record_id", "amount", "target"}
if not required.issubset(df.columns) or df.empty:
    raise ValueError("missing columns or empty dataset")
if df["record_id"].isna().any() or df["record_id"].duplicated().any():
    raise ValueError("invalid record ids")
if not is_numeric_dtype(df["amount"]) or not df["amount"].dropna().between(0, 1000).all():
    raise ValueError("amount outside the toy contract")
if not df["target"].isin([0, 1]).all():
    raise ValueError("target must be 0 or 1")
```

- limits must come from the task, not a universal rule; the amount range above is only an example
- use exceptions for required runtime checks; python assertions can be disabled
- larger validation suites can express checks as reusable expectations and record their results [great expectations](https://docs.greatexpectations.io/docs/core/define_expectations/)

## prevent leakage

- define the prediction time; exclude features only available after that time
- fit imputation, scaling, and feature selection on training folds only
- split by entity when evaluating generalisation to unseen people or accounts; use time-aware splits for future prediction
- use point-in-time joins so historical features reflect what was available then, including arrival delays [point-in-time retrieval](https://docs.feast.dev/getting-started/concepts/point-in-time-joins)
- pipelines help with preprocessing leakage, but cannot repair an inappropriate split or a leaked target [scikit-learn pitfalls](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html)

## group split plus preprocessing

- given a larger labelled `df` with repeated `entity_id` values, this holds out whole entities for validation [group split documentation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.model_selection.GroupShuffleSplit.html)

```python
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.model_selection import GroupShuffleSplit
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

splitter = GroupShuffleSplit(n_splits=1, test_size=0.2, random_state=42)
train, val = next(splitter.split(df, groups=df["entity_id"]))
pipeline = make_pipeline(
    SimpleImputer(strategy="median"), StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression()
)
pipeline.fit(df.iloc[train][["amount"]], df.iloc[train]["target"])
probabilities = pipeline.predict_proba(df.iloc[val][["amount"]])[:, 1]
```

- check class coverage in each split; group splitting does not guarantee stratification
- keep a separate final test set before model selection; this snippet only demonstrates a training/validation split
